rules.rule_name: New Session Detection and Sign-On Redirect
rules.rule_description: When a user attempts to access the Admin Menu without an active session context, the system redirects them to the Sign-On screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Session Active?
EIBCALEN = 0?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user attempts to access the Admin Menu program
acceptance_criteria.When: No active session context exists (communication area length is zero)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the origin program to 'COSGN00C' and redirects the user to the Sign-On screen

rules.rule_name: First-Time Admin Menu Entry Initialization
rules.rule_description: On the first entry into the Admin Menu program within an active session, the screen is initialized with blank/default values before being displayed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
First Time Entry?
CDEMO-PGM-REENTER?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has an active session and navigates to the Admin Menu for the first time
acceptance_criteria.When: The program detects it has not been previously entered (CDEMO-PGM-REENTER is not set)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program marks itself as re-enterable (sets CDEMO-PGM-REENTER to TRUE), initializes the Admin Menu screen output area with LOW-VALUES (blank defaults), and sends the Admin Menu screen to the user

rules.rule_name: Admin Menu Screen Rendering
rules.rule_description: The Admin Menu screen is fully rebuilt and sent to the user each time it needs to be displayed, including header information, menu options, and any messages.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
3:Admin Menu Screen Rendering
Build and Send Admin Menu Screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Admin Menu screen needs to be displayed to the user
acceptance_criteria.When: A send menu screen action is triggered (on first entry, after validation error, after invalid key, or after uninstalled option selection)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system populates the header information, builds the menu options list, moves any pending message to the error message field on screen, and sends the complete Admin Menu screen (map 'COADM1A' from mapset 'COADM01') to the user, erasing any previous screen content

rules.rule_name: Screen Header Information Population
rules.rule_description: Each time the Admin Menu screen is displayed, the header is populated with current date, current time, application titles, transaction ID, and program name.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
4:Header Information Population
Date MM/DD/YY, Time HH:MM:SS
Title, TransID, ProgramName

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Admin Menu screen is being prepared for display
acceptance_criteria.When: The header population step is executed
acceptance_criteria.Then: The screen header is populated with: the current date formatted as MM/DD/YY, the current time formatted as HH:MM:SS, the first application title (CCDA-TITLE01), the second application title (CCDA-TITLE02), the current transaction ID (WS-TRANID), and the current program name (WS-PGMNAME)

rules.rule_name: Admin Menu Options Construction
rules.rule_description: The Admin Menu dynamically builds and displays up to 10 menu options, each formatted with its option number and name.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
5:Menu Options Construction
Build up to 10 Admin Menu Options

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Admin Menu screen is being prepared for display
acceptance_criteria.When: The menu options construction step is executed
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system iterates through all available admin options (up to the total count defined in CDEMO-ADMIN-OPT-COUNT), formats each option as '[Option Number]. [Option Name]', and places each formatted option into the corresponding display field (OPTN001O through OPTN010O); any options beyond position 10 are not displayed

rules.rule_name: User Input Capture from Admin Menu Screen
rules.rule_description: When a returning user submits the Admin Menu screen, the system captures all input entered by the user.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
6:User Input Capture
Receive Admin Menu Screen Input

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has an active session and has previously been shown the Admin Menu screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The user submits the screen (presses any key)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system receives and captures the user's input from the Admin Menu screen (map 'COADM1A' from mapset 'COADM01') into the input area (COADM1AI) for further processing

rules.rule_name: Enter Key Processing - Option Input Normalization
rules.rule_description: When the user presses Enter, the system reads and normalizes the entered option value by trimming trailing spaces and converting blank input to zero.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
7:Enter Key Processing
Read entered option value

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has submitted the Admin Menu screen by pressing the Enter key
acceptance_criteria.When: The system processes the Enter key action
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system scans the option input field (OPTIONI of COADM1AI) from right to left to find the last non-space character, extracts the meaningful portion of the input into WS-OPTION-X, replaces any remaining spaces within that value with '0' (so a fully blank entry becomes '0'), moves the normalized value to WS-OPTION, and displays the normalized value back in the option output field (OPTIONO of COADM1AO)

rules.rule_name: Menu Option Validation
rules.rule_description: The entered menu option is validated to ensure it is numeric, non-zero, and within the range of available admin menu options.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
8:Menu Option Validation
Check numeric, non-zero, within range

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has pressed Enter and the option input has been normalized
acceptance_criteria.When: The system validates the entered option value (WS-OPTION)
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the option is not numeric, OR the option value exceeds the total number of available admin options (CDEMO-ADMIN-OPT-COUNT), OR the option equals zero, then the system sets the error flag (WS-ERR-FLG to 'Y') and displays the error message 'Please enter a valid option number...' on the Admin Menu screen; otherwise the option is considered valid and processing continues

rules.rule_name: Installed Program Navigation
rules.rule_description: When a valid, installed admin menu option is selected, the system transfers control to the corresponding program, passing the current session context.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
9:Navigate to Selected Admin Function
Transfer control to selected program
with COMMAREA

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has entered a valid menu option and the corresponding program is installed (program name does not start with 'DUMMY')
acceptance_criteria.When: The system processes the valid option selection
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system records the current transaction ID (WS-TRANID) as the originating transaction (CDEMO-FROM-TRANID), records the current program name (WS-PGMNAME) as the originating program (CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM), resets the program context to zero (CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT), and transfers control to the selected admin option's program (CDEMO-ADMIN-OPT-PGMNAME for the chosen option) passing the full session communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA)

rules.rule_name: Uninstalled Option Handling
rules.rule_description: When a user selects a valid menu option number that corresponds to a program not yet installed (marked as DUMMY), the system informs the user and keeps them on the Admin Menu.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
10:Uninstalled Option Handling
Display green info message:
This option is not installed

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has entered a valid menu option number and no validation errors exist
acceptance_criteria.When: The program name associated with the selected option starts with 'DUMMY' (indicating the feature is not yet installed)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the error message color to green (DFHGREEN), constructs the message 'This option is not installed...' and displays it on the Admin Menu screen, keeping the user on the Admin Menu

rules.rule_name: PF3 Key - Return to Sign-On Screen
rules.rule_description: When the user presses PF3 on the Admin Menu, the system exits the Admin Menu and returns the user to the Sign-On screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
11:Return to Sign-On Screen
PF3 pressed - Transfer to COSGN00C

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user is on the Admin Menu screen with an active session
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses the PF3 key
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the target program to 'COSGN00C' (Sign-On screen) and transfers control to the Sign-On program; if no target program is explicitly set, the system defaults to 'COSGN00C'

rules.rule_name: Invalid Key Handling
rules.rule_description: When the user presses any key other than Enter or PF3 on the Admin Menu, the system displays an invalid key error and redisplays the menu.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
12:Invalid Key Handling
Display error: Use valid key

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user is on the Admin Menu screen with an active session
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses any key other than Enter (DFHENTER) or PF3 (DFHPF3)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag (WS-ERR-FLG to 'Y'), populates the error message with the standard invalid key message (CCDA-MSG-INVALID-KEY) from WS-MESSAGE, and redisplays the Admin Menu screen

rules.rule_name: Missing Program Error Handling
rules.rule_description: If the system cannot locate a selected program during transfer of control, the user is informed the option is not installed and is returned to the Admin Menu.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
13:Missing Program Error Handling
PGMIDERR - Display green info message:
This option is not installed

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has selected an admin menu option and the system attempted to transfer control to the associated program
acceptance_criteria.When: The system cannot find the specified program (a program-not-found error condition is raised)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system clears the message area, sets the message color to green (DFHGREEN), constructs the message 'This option is not installed...' into WS-MESSAGE, redisplays the Admin Menu screen, and returns control to the same Admin Menu transaction passing the current session communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA), keeping the user on the Admin Menu

rules.rule_name: Verify Active User Session Before Accessing Admin Menu
rules.rule_description: When a user attempts to access the Admin Menu, the system must verify that an active session exists by checking whether a communication area was passed. If no session context is present, the user must be redirected to authenticate via the Sign-On screen before proceeding.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is an Active User Session Present?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user attempts to access the Admin Menu
acceptance_criteria.When: No active session context (communication area) is present from a prior transaction
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must deny access to the Admin Menu and initiate a redirect to the Sign-On screen, recording 'COSGN00C' as the originating program before transferring control

rules.rule_name: Validate Sign-On Destination Before Redirecting Unauthenticated User
rules.rule_description: Before redirecting an unauthenticated user to the Sign-On screen, the system must verify whether a target Sign-On destination program has already been specified in the session context. If the destination is undefined or blank, a default must be assigned to ensure the redirect succeeds.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is Sign-On Destination Defined?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has determined that no active session exists and must redirect the user to the Sign-On screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The target destination program field (CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM) contains low-values or spaces, indicating it has not been set
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must recognize the destination as undefined and proceed to assign the default Sign-On program before executing the redirect

rules.rule_name: Assign Default Sign-On Screen as Redirect Destination
rules.rule_description: When no Sign-On destination has been explicitly defined in the session context, the system must automatically default the redirect target to the standard Sign-On screen program ('COSGN00C') to ensure the unauthenticated user is always directed to a valid authentication entry point.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Default Destination Set to Sign-On Screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has determined that the target destination program (CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM) is undefined (contains low-values or spaces)
acceptance_criteria.When: A default destination needs to be established for the Sign-On redirect
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must set the target destination program to 'COSGN00C' (the standard Sign-On screen) as the default redirect target

rules.rule_name: Redirect Unauthenticated User to Sign-On Screen
rules.rule_description: Once the Sign-On destination has been confirmed or defaulted, the system must transfer full control to the Sign-On screen program, requiring the user to authenticate before any access to the Admin Menu is granted. This ensures no unauthenticated user can bypass the login process.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Redirect User to Sign-On Screen to Authenticate

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has confirmed or assigned the Sign-On destination program (CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM is set to 'COSGN00C' or another valid Sign-On program name)
acceptance_criteria.When: The redirect to the Sign-On screen is executed
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must transfer full control to the Sign-On destination program (CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM), terminating the current Admin Menu transaction and requiring the user to authenticate

rules.rule_name: Load Session Context and Proceed to Admin Menu for Authenticated User
rules.rule_description: When an active session context is present, confirming the user has an established session, the system must load the full session communication area and allow the user to proceed to the Admin Menu without interruption.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Proceed to Admin Menu

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user attempts to access the Admin Menu
acceptance_criteria.When: An active session context (communication area) is present from a prior transaction, confirming the user has an established session
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must load the complete session context (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) from the passed communication area and allow the user to proceed to the Admin Menu processing flow

rules.rule_name: Detect First-Time Entry to Admin Menu
rules.rule_description: Determines whether the user is visiting the Admin Menu for the first time within an active session, distinguishing between an initial display and a subsequent re-entry after user interaction.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Detect First-Time Entry
Session exists but screen not yet shown

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has an active session (communication area is present with session context loaded) and the Admin Menu program has not yet been displayed to the user in this session (the re-entry flag CDEMO-PGM-REENTER is not set to TRUE)
acceptance_criteria.When: The Admin Menu program is invoked and the session context is evaluated to determine if this is the first time the program is being entered
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system identifies this as a first-time entry and proceeds to initialize and display the Admin Menu screen for the first time

rules.rule_name: Mark Admin Menu Session as Re-Enterable
rules.rule_description: Once the Admin Menu is displayed for the first time, the session is flagged so that subsequent returns to this program (e.g., after an invalid key press or option error) do not re-initialize the screen, preserving the user's context.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Mark Session as Re-Entry
Prevent re-initialization on next visit

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has confirmed this is the first-time entry to the Admin Menu within the active session
acceptance_criteria.When: The Admin Menu is about to be displayed for the first time
acceptance_criteria.Then: The session re-entry flag (CDEMO-PGM-REENTER) is set to TRUE so that any future return to this program within the same session is treated as a re-entry and not a fresh initialization

rules.rule_name: Clear Admin Menu Screen Before Display
rules.rule_description: Before populating and displaying the Admin Menu for the first time, all screen output fields are reset to their lowest binary values (empty/blank), ensuring no residual data from prior transactions appears on the screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Clear Admin Menu Screen
Reset all screen fields to empty

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has confirmed this is the first-time entry to the Admin Menu and the session re-entry flag has been set
acceptance_criteria.When: The Admin Menu screen is being prepared for its initial display
acceptance_criteria.Then: All fields of the Admin Menu screen output area (COADM1AO) are reset to LOW-VALUES (empty), clearing any previously held data before the screen is populated with fresh content

rules.rule_name: Populate Admin Menu Screen Header with Current Date and Time
rules.rule_description: The Admin Menu screen header is populated with the current system date and time, the application title lines, the active transaction identifier, and the current program name, providing the user with contextual information about their session.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Populate Screen Header
Date, Time, Application Title
Transaction ID, Program Name

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Admin Menu screen is being prepared for display and the screen area has been cleared
acceptance_criteria.When: The screen header population step is executed
acceptance_criteria.Then: The screen header is populated with: (1) Application Title Line 1 (CCDA-TITLE01) displayed in the TITLE01O field, (2) Application Title Line 2 (CCDA-TITLE02) displayed in the TITLE02O field, (3) Current Transaction ID (WS-TRANID) displayed in the TRNNAMEO field, (4) Current Program Name (WS-PGMNAME) displayed in the PGMNAMEO field, (5) Current system date formatted as MM/DD/YY displayed in the CURDATEO field, and (6) Current system time formatted as HH:MM:SS displayed in the CURTIMEO field

rules.rule_name: Build and Format Admin Menu Option List
rules.rule_description: Each available administrative menu option is formatted by combining its option number and option name into a single display string, then placed into the corresponding screen option field. A maximum of 10 options can be displayed; any options beyond 10 are excluded from the screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Build Admin Menu Options
Combine Option Number and Option Name
for each available admin option

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Admin Menu screen header has been populated and the total count of available admin options (CDEMO-ADMIN-OPT-COUNT) is known
acceptance_criteria.When: The system iterates through each available admin option from 1 up to the total admin option count
acceptance_criteria.Then: For each option (index 1 through the total count): the option display text is constructed by concatenating the option number (CDEMO-ADMIN-OPT-NUM), the literal '. ', and the option name (CDEMO-ADMIN-OPT-NAME) into a single text string; this formatted text is then placed into the corresponding screen output field (OPTN001O through OPTN010O) based on the option's position; options at positions 1 through 10 are displayed in their respective fields; any options beyond position 10 are not displayed on the screen

rules.rule_name: Display Fully Populated Admin Menu Screen to User
rules.rule_description: After the screen header and all menu options have been populated, the complete Admin Menu screen is sent to the user's terminal, erasing any prior screen content and presenting the fresh menu awaiting user input.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Display Admin Menu Screen
Present fully populated menu
to the user

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Admin Menu screen output area (COADM1AO) has been fully populated with the header information, all available menu options, and any applicable message in the error message field (ERRMSGO)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system sends the Admin Menu screen to the user's terminal
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Admin Menu screen (map COADM1A from mapset COADM01) is displayed to the user with the ERASE option active, which clears the entire terminal screen before presenting the newly populated Admin Menu, and the user is presented with the complete list of administrative options awaiting their selection

rules.rule_name: Retrieve Current System Date and Time for Screen Display
rules.rule_description: When the Admin Menu screen is being prepared for display, the system retrieves the current date and time to populate the screen header with up-to-date information.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Retrieve Current System Date and Time

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Admin Menu screen rendering process has been initiated
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares the screen header information
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system retrieves the current system date and time and stores it in the working date/time data fields (WS-CURDATE-DATA) for subsequent formatting and display on the screen header

rules.rule_name: Format Current Date as MM/DD/YY for Screen Header
rules.rule_description: The retrieved system date must be formatted into MM/DD/YY format before being placed on the Admin Menu screen header.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Format Date as MM/DD/YY

acceptance_criteria.Given: The current system date has been retrieved and is available in the working date fields
acceptance_criteria.When: The system formats the date for screen display
acceptance_criteria.Then: The month portion is placed in the MM position, the day portion is placed in the DD position, and only the last two digits of the year are placed in the YY position, resulting in a date displayed as MM/DD/YY in the screen header date field (CURDATEO)

rules.rule_name: Format Current Time as HH:MM:SS for Screen Header
rules.rule_description: The retrieved system time must be formatted into HH:MM:SS format before being placed on the Admin Menu screen header.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Format Time as HH:MM:SS

acceptance_criteria.Given: The current system time has been retrieved and is available in the working time fields
acceptance_criteria.When: The system formats the time for screen display
acceptance_criteria.Then: The hours portion is placed in the HH position, the minutes portion is placed in the MM position, and the seconds portion is placed in the SS position, resulting in a time displayed as HH:MM:SS in the screen header time field (CURTIMEO)

rules.rule_name: Populate Application Titles on Admin Menu Screen Header
rules.rule_description: The Admin Menu screen header must display the two standard application title lines sourced from the application's central configuration data.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Populate Application Titles on Screen Header

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Admin Menu screen is being prepared for display and application title values are available in the application configuration (CCDA-TITLE01 and CCDA-TITLE02)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system populates the screen header fields
acceptance_criteria.Then: Application Title Line 1 (CCDA-TITLE01) is placed into the first title field (TITLE01O) on the screen header, and Application Title Line 2 (CCDA-TITLE02) is placed into the second title field (TITLE02O) on the screen header

rules.rule_name: Populate Transaction ID on Admin Menu Screen Header
rules.rule_description: The Admin Menu screen header must display the current transaction identifier so the user can see which transaction they are operating under.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Populate Transaction ID on Screen Header

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Admin Menu screen is being prepared for display and the current transaction ID is available (WS-TRANID)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system populates the screen header fields
acceptance_criteria.Then: The current transaction ID (WS-TRANID) is placed into the transaction name field (TRNNAMEO) on the screen header

rules.rule_name: Populate Program Name on Admin Menu Screen Header
rules.rule_description: The Admin Menu screen header must display the current program name so the user can identify which program they are currently interacting with.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Populate Program Name on Screen Header

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Admin Menu screen is being prepared for display and the current program name is available (WS-PGMNAME)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system populates the screen header fields
acceptance_criteria.Then: The current program name (WS-PGMNAME) is placed into the program name field (PGMNAMEO) on the screen header

rules.rule_name: Iterate Through All Available Admin Menu Options for Display
rules.rule_description: The system must iterate through all configured admin menu options, starting from option 1, and continue until all options defined in the admin option count have been processed for display.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Begin Building Menu Options
Start from Option 1

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Admin Menu screen is being built and the total count of available admin options is defined in CDEMO-ADMIN-OPT-COUNT
acceptance_criteria.When: The system begins building the menu option list
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system starts from option index 1 and increments by 1 for each iteration, continuing until the index exceeds the total admin option count (CDEMO-ADMIN-OPT-COUNT), ensuring every configured option is processed for display

rules.rule_name: Combine Option Number and Option Name into Formatted Display Text
rules.rule_description: For each admin menu option, the option number and option name must be combined into a single formatted display string in the format '[Number]. [Name]'.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Combine Option Number and Option Name into Display Text

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is processing a menu option at the current index (WS-IDX) and both the option number (CDEMO-ADMIN-OPT-NUM) and option name (CDEMO-ADMIN-OPT-NAME) are available for that index

rules.rule_name: Place Formatted Option Text into Corresponding Screen Field for Options 1 Through 10

rules.rule_name: Display Error or Informational Message on Admin Menu Screen

rules.rule_name: Send Completed Admin Menu Screen to User with Full Screen Refresh

acceptance_criteria.Given: All screen fields including header information, menu options, and any messages have been populated in the screen output area (COADM1AO)

rules.rule_name: Place Formatted Date MM/DD/YY onto Admin Menu Screen

rules.rule_name: Iterate Through All Configured Admin Menu Options
rules.rule_description: The menu construction process starts at the first configured admin option and continues iterating through each option sequentially until all configured admin options have been processed. The total number of options is governed by the configured admin options count.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Begin with Option Index = 1 / More Options to Display? Index exceeds total admin options count?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Admin Menu screen is being prepared for display and the total count of configured administrative menu options (CDEMO-ADMIN-OPT-COUNT) is known
acceptance_criteria.When: The menu options construction process begins, starting from option index 1 and incrementing by 1 on each cycle
acceptance_criteria.Then: The process continues building and placing each option onto the screen for every index from 1 up to and including the total configured admin options count; once the index exceeds the total count, the construction process ends and all built options are ready for screen display

rules.rule_name: Clear Option Text Area Before Building Each Menu Entry
rules.rule_description: Before constructing the display text for each menu option, the option text working area must be cleared to spaces to ensure no residual data from a previous option contaminates the current option's display text.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Clear Option Text Area

acceptance_criteria.Given: The menu options construction loop is processing a specific admin option at the current index
acceptance_criteria.When: A new iteration begins for any option index within the configured admin options count
acceptance_criteria.Then: The option text working area (WS-ADMIN-OPT-TXT) is reset to spaces before any new text is written into it, ensuring a clean slate for the current option's formatted display text

rules.rule_name: Format Each Menu Option as Number Followed by Name
rules.rule_description: Each administrative menu option must be displayed in a standardized format that combines the option's sequence number, a period and space separator, and the option's descriptive name into a single line of display text.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Combine Option Number + '. ' + Option Name into single display text

acceptance_criteria.Given: The option text area has been cleared and the current option index points to a valid configured admin option with an option number (CDEMO-ADMIN-OPT-NUM) and an option name (CDEMO-ADMIN-OPT-NAME)
acceptance_criteria.When: The display text is being constructed for the current admin option
acceptance_criteria.Then: The formatted display text is built by concatenating: the option number (CDEMO-ADMIN-OPT-NUM for the current index), followed by the literal '. ' (period and space), followed by the option name (CDEMO-ADMIN-OPT-NAME for the current index), all stored into the option text working area (WS-ADMIN-OPT-TXT)

rules.rule_name: Place Formatted Option Text into the Correct Screen Display Slot
rules.rule_description: Once the formatted display text for a menu option is ready, it must be placed into the correct numbered display slot on the Admin Menu screen. Each option index from 1 to 10 maps to a dedicated screen output field.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Which Option Number is it? 1 through 10 / Place formatted text into Option Slot 1 through 10

acceptance_criteria.Given: The formatted display text (WS-ADMIN-OPT-TXT) has been constructed for the current admin option and the current option index (WS-IDX) is between 1 and 10 inclusive
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the current option index to determine which screen slot to populate
acceptance_criteria.Then: The formatted text is placed into the corresponding screen output field: index 1 maps to OPTN001O, index 2 maps to OPTN002O, index 3 maps to OPTN003O, index 4 maps to OPTN004O, index 5 maps to OPTN005O, index 6 maps to OPTN006O, index 7 maps to OPTN007O, index 8 maps to OPTN008O, index 9 maps to OPTN009O, and index 10 maps to OPTN010O

rules.rule_name: Silently Ignore Admin Options Beyond the Tenth Position
rules.rule_description: The Admin Menu screen supports a maximum of 10 displayable option slots. Any configured admin option with an index greater than 10 is silently skipped and not displayed on the screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Which Option Number is it? 1 through 10

acceptance_criteria.Given: The menu options construction loop is processing a configured admin option whose index (WS-IDX) is greater than 10
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the current option index and it does not match any value from 1 through 10
acceptance_criteria.Then: No action is taken for that option — it is not placed into any screen display slot and the loop simply advances to the next index; the Admin Menu screen can display a maximum of 10 options only

rules.rule_name: Advance to Next Option After Placing Current Option on Screen
rules.rule_description: After the formatted text for the current admin option has been placed into its designated screen slot (or skipped if beyond slot 10), the process must advance to the next option in the configured list by incrementing the option index.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Move to Next Option / Increment Index by 1

acceptance_criteria.Given: The current admin option at the active index has been processed (formatted and placed into its screen slot, or skipped if index exceeds 10)
acceptance_criteria.When: The current iteration of the menu construction loop completes
acceptance_criteria.Then: The option index (WS-IDX) is incremented by 1 and the loop condition is re-evaluated to determine whether more configured admin options remain to be processed

rules.rule_name: Display Admin Menu Screen on First Entry
rules.rule_description: On the first entry into the Admin Menu program, the system initializes the screen with blank/default values and displays the Admin Menu to the user, awaiting their interaction.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Display Admin Menu Screen
Awaiting User Interaction

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has an active session with a valid communication area, AND the Admin Menu program is being entered for the first time (the re-entry flag CDEMO-PGM-REENTER is NOT set)
acceptance_criteria.When: The program detects it is the first entry (NOT CDEMO-PGM-REENTER is TRUE)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system marks the session as re-enterable (sets CDEMO-PGM-REENTER to TRUE), clears the Admin Menu output area to blank/default values (LOW-VALUES), and sends the Admin Menu screen (MAP COADM1A, MAPSET COADM01) to the user for display, erasing any previous screen content

rules.rule_name: Capture User Input from Admin Menu Screen on Re-Entry
rules.rule_description: When the user returns to the Admin Menu program after the screen has already been displayed (re-entry), the system captures all input entered by the user — including the option number typed — from the Admin Menu screen into the Admin Menu Input Area (COADM1AI) for further processing.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Capture All Screen Input
into Admin Menu Input Area

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has an active session with a valid communication area, AND the Admin Menu screen has already been displayed to the user (CDEMO-PGM-REENTER is TRUE), AND the user has typed an option number and pressed a key
acceptance_criteria.When: The program detects it is a re-entry (CDEMO-PGM-REENTER is TRUE) and invokes the screen receive operation
acceptance_criteria.Then: All screen input data, including the option number entered by the user in the OPTIONI field, is captured from the Admin Menu screen (MAP COADM1A, MAPSET COADM01) and stored into the Admin Menu Input Area (COADM1AI), making the OPTIONI field available for further processing

rules.rule_name: Identify Key Pressed by User After Input Capture
rules.rule_description: After the user's screen input is captured, the system evaluates which key the user pressed (Enter, PF3, or any other key) to determine the appropriate next action to take.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
User Presses a Key
Enter / PF3 / Other

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user's screen input has been successfully captured into the Admin Menu Input Area (COADM1AI), AND the key pressed by the user is recorded in the EIBAID field
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the EIBAID field to determine which key was pressed
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the user pressed the ENTER key, the system proceeds to process the selected menu option (PROCESS-ENTER-KEY); if the user pressed PF3, the system sets the target program to the Sign-On screen (COSGN00C) and navigates there; if the user pressed any other key, the system sets the error flag (WS-ERR-FLG = 'Y'), loads the invalid key error message (CCDA-MSG-INVALID-KEY) into WS-MESSAGE, and redisplays the Admin Menu screen with the error message

rules.rule_name: Option Number Field Available for Processing After Input Capture
rules.rule_description: Once the screen input is captured, the option number entered by the user in the OPTIONI field of the Admin Menu Input Area is available and is extracted (with trailing spaces stripped) into a working variable for validation and navigation processing.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Option Number Field
OPTIONI is Now Available
for Further Processing

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user's screen input has been captured into the Admin Menu Input Area (COADM1AI), AND the user pressed the ENTER key
acceptance_criteria.When: The system processes the Enter key action and begins extracting the option number from the OPTIONI field of COADM1AI
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system scans the OPTIONI field from right to left to find the last non-space character, extracts the meaningful portion of the option input (from position 1 to the last non-space character index WS-IDX) into the working variable WS-OPTION-X, making the entered option number available for subsequent validation and menu navigation

rules.rule_name: Read User Entered Option from Admin Menu Screen
rules.rule_description: When the user presses Enter on the Admin Menu screen, the system reads the option value entered by the user from the menu input field and captures it for further processing.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Read User Entered Option
from Admin Menu Screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Admin Menu screen is displayed and the user has typed a value into the option input field
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses the Enter key to submit their menu selection
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system reads the value entered by the user from the Admin Menu option input field and makes it available for cleaning and validation

rules.rule_name: Trim Trailing Spaces from Entered Option Value
rules.rule_description: The system removes trailing spaces from the user-entered option value by scanning the input from right to left and identifying the last meaningful (non-space) character position, so that only the significant portion of the input is retained.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Trim Trailing Spaces
from Entered Option Value
Scan from right until non-space found

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user-entered option value has been read from the Admin Menu screen input field and may contain trailing spaces
acceptance_criteria.When: The system processes the entered option value to prepare it for validation
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system scans the entered option value from the rightmost character position backwards, stopping at the first non-space character or at position 1 (whichever comes first), and retains only the characters from position 1 up to and including that last non-space character position

rules.rule_name: Replace Remaining Internal Spaces with Zeros in Option Value
rules.rule_description: After trimming trailing spaces, any spaces that remain within the retained portion of the option value (including a fully blank entry) are replaced with zeros, ensuring that a blank or empty entry is treated as the value zero rather than as missing data.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Replace Any Remaining
Spaces with Zeros
in Option Value

acceptance_criteria.Given: The trailing spaces have been trimmed from the user-entered option value and the significant portion of the input has been extracted
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares the option value for validation
acceptance_criteria.Then: Every space character remaining in the extracted option value is replaced with the character '0', so that a completely blank entry becomes '0' and any partially blank entry has its spaces filled with zeros

rules.rule_name: Store Cleaned Option Value and Echo to Display
rules.rule_description: Once the option value has been trimmed and normalized, the cleaned value is stored as the active option for validation and is also echoed back to the Admin Menu screen's option display field so the user can see exactly what value the system has captured.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Store Cleaned Option Value
Ready for Validation

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user-entered option value has been trimmed of trailing spaces and all remaining spaces have been replaced with zeros
acceptance_criteria.When: The system finalizes preparation of the option value
acceptance_criteria.Then: The cleaned and normalized option value is stored as the working option value ready for validation, and the same cleaned value is also written back to the option display field on the Admin Menu screen so the user sees the interpreted value

rules.rule_name: Initialize Option Scan Position to Last Character
rules.rule_description: When a user enters a menu option value, the system must begin scanning from the rightmost (last) character position of the entered option field to identify where meaningful input ends and trailing spaces begin.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set Scan Position to Last Character of Entered Option

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has entered a value in the Admin Menu option input field, and the system is about to process the entered option
acceptance_criteria.When: The system begins the trailing-space trimming process for the entered option value
acceptance_criteria.Then: The scan position is initialized to the full length of the entered option input field (i.e., the last character position), so that scanning proceeds from right to left

rules.rule_name: Scan Left to Find Last Non-Space Character in Entered Option
rules.rule_description: The system scans the entered option value from right to left, moving the scan position one step left for each trailing space found, stopping either when a non-space character is encountered or when the beginning of the field (position 1) is reached. This ensures that only meaningful input is retained.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is Current Character a Space AND Position Greater than 1?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The scan position is set to the last character of the entered option input field, and the system is scanning leftward to find the last non-space character
acceptance_criteria.When: The character at the current scan position is a space AND the current scan position is greater than 1
acceptance_criteria.Then: The scan position is moved one step to the left, and the check is repeated; scanning stops when either a non-space character is found at the current position OR the scan position reaches position 1 (the beginning of the field)

rules.rule_name: Extract Trimmed Option Value Up to Last Non-Space Position
rules.rule_description: Once the rightmost non-space character position is identified, the system extracts the option value from the first character up to and including that position, effectively removing all trailing spaces from the entered option.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Extract Option Value from Position 1 up to Current Scan Position

acceptance_criteria.Given: The scan has completed and the current scan position points to either the last non-space character or position 1 of the entered option field
acceptance_criteria.When: The system extracts the option value
acceptance_criteria.Then: The option value is extracted from position 1 through the current scan position of the entered option input field, and this trimmed value is stored as the working option value for further processing

rules.rule_name: Treat Blank or Whitespace-Only Option Entry as Zero
rules.rule_description: After trimming, if the extracted option value still contains any spaces (e.g., the user entered only spaces or left the field blank), each remaining space character is replaced with '0', so that a blank or whitespace-only entry is treated as the numeric value zero for subsequent validation.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Extract Option Value from Position 1 up to Current Scan Position

acceptance_criteria.Given: The trimmed option value has been extracted from the entered option input field and stored as the working option value

rules.rule_name: Replace Remaining Spaces with Zeros in Menu Option Input
rules.rule_description: After capturing and trimming the user's menu option input, any spaces that still remain within the option value must be replaced with zeros. This ensures that a partially blank or whitespace-padded entry is normalized to a numeric-looking value before validation. For example, a single character entered as '1 ' becomes '10' after replacement.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Any Spaces Remaining in Option Value? → Replace All Spaces with Zeros in Option Value

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has entered a menu option value on the Admin Menu screen, and the trailing-space trimming step has already been performed, resulting in a captured option value stored in the working option input field (WS-OPTION-X)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system inspects the captured option input field (WS-OPTION-X) and finds one or more space characters remaining anywhere within the value
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system replaces every space character found in the option input field (WS-OPTION-X) with the character zero ('0'), so that the entire field contains no spaces and is fully normalized for numeric validation

rules.rule_name: No Spaces Present — Option Value Passes Through Unchanged
rules.rule_description: If the captured menu option input contains no remaining spaces after the trimming step, the value is already clean and requires no replacement. It is passed directly to the next step for storage and validation without modification.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Any Spaces Remaining in Option Value? → No - No Spaces → Store Cleaned Option Value Ready for Validation

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has entered a menu option value on the Admin Menu screen, and the trailing-space trimming step has already been performed, resulting in a captured option value stored in the working option input field (WS-OPTION-X)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system inspects the captured option input field (WS-OPTION-X) and finds no space characters remaining within the value
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system leaves the option input field (WS-OPTION-X) unchanged and proceeds directly to store the value as the cleaned option ready for validation

rules.rule_name: Store Cleaned Option Value as the Active Selection for Validation
rules.rule_description: Once the option input has been normalized (spaces replaced with zeros where applicable), the cleaned value must be stored into the active menu option field (WS-OPTION). This field is the definitive value that will be used in all subsequent validation checks to determine whether the user's selection is a valid admin menu option.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Store Cleaned Option Value Ready for Validation

acceptance_criteria.Given: The menu option input field (WS-OPTION-X) has been fully normalized — trailing spaces trimmed and any remaining spaces replaced with zeros
acceptance_criteria.When: The system is ready to proceed to option validation
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system copies the cleaned and normalized option value from the working input field (WS-OPTION-X) into the active option selection field (WS-OPTION), making it the definitive value to be used for all validation and navigation logic

rules.rule_name: Display Cleaned Option Value Back on the Admin Menu Screen
rules.rule_description: After the option value has been cleaned and stored, the normalized value must be reflected back on the Admin Menu screen in the option display field. This ensures the user sees exactly what value the system has recorded as their selection, providing transparency and consistency between what was entered and what will be processed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display Cleaned Option Value Back on Screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: The cleaned and normalized menu option value has been stored in the active option selection field (WS-OPTION)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares to display or redisplay the Admin Menu screen
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system moves the cleaned option value from the active option selection field (WS-OPTION) into the screen output option display field (OPTIONO of COADM1AO), so that the user sees the normalized value that the system will use for validation and processing

rules.rule_name: Capture and Normalize Admin Menu Option Input
rules.rule_description: When a user submits the Admin Menu screen, the entered option value is captured from the screen input field, trailing spaces are removed, and any remaining spaces within the value are replaced with zeros to produce a clean, normalized option value for validation.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Capture User Entered Option from Admin Menu Screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has submitted the Admin Menu screen by pressing the Enter key, and the option input field (OPTIONI) contains a value that may include trailing or embedded spaces
acceptance_criteria.When: The system processes the submitted screen input by scanning the option field from right to left to find the last non-space character, extracting the meaningful portion of the input, and replacing any remaining spaces within that extracted value with the character '0'
acceptance_criteria.Then: The normalized option value is stored as the working option (WS-OPTION) and is also reflected back on the Admin Menu screen output field (OPTIONO) so the user can see what was interpreted from their entry

rules.rule_name: Admin Menu Option Must Be Numeric
rules.rule_description: The Admin Menu option entered by the user must consist entirely of numeric characters. Non-numeric input is rejected immediately with an error message and the menu is redisplayed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is Entered Option Numeric?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has entered a value in the Admin Menu option field and pressed Enter, and the system has normalized the input value into WS-OPTION
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates whether WS-OPTION contains only numeric characters (IS NOT NUMERIC condition is checked)
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the option value is not numeric, the system sets the error flag (WS-ERR-FLG = 'Y'), populates the error message with 'Please enter a valid option number...', and redisplays the Admin Menu screen with the error message shown to the user

rules.rule_name: Admin Menu Option Must Not Be Zero
rules.rule_description: The Admin Menu option entered by the user must not be zero. A zero value — which also results from a blank or empty entry after normalization — is not a valid menu selection and is rejected with an error message.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is Entered Option Zero?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has entered a value in the Admin Menu option field and pressed Enter, the input has been normalized, and the value has passed the numeric check
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates whether WS-OPTION equals zero (WS-OPTION = ZEROS condition is checked), which includes the case where the user left the field blank (blank input is normalized to '0')
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the option value equals zero, the system sets the error flag (WS-ERR-FLG = 'Y'), populates the error message with 'Please enter a valid option number...', and redisplays the Admin Menu screen with the error message shown to the user

rules.rule_name: Admin Menu Option Must Be Within the Valid Range of Available Options
rules.rule_description: The Admin Menu option entered by the user must not exceed the total number of administrative options currently configured and available in the system. Options beyond the defined count are not valid selections.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is Entered Option Within Valid Range of Available Admin Options?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has entered a numeric, non-zero value in the Admin Menu option field and pressed Enter, and the system has a defined count of available administrative options (CDEMO-ADMIN-OPT-COUNT)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates whether WS-OPTION is greater than the total count of available administrative options (WS-OPTION > CDEMO-ADMIN-OPT-COUNT)
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the option value exceeds the available option count, the system sets the error flag (WS-ERR-FLG = 'Y'), populates the error message with 'Please enter a valid option number...', and redisplays the Admin Menu screen with the error message shown to the user

rules.rule_name: Combined Admin Menu Option Validation with Single Error Response
rules.rule_description: All three option validation conditions — non-numeric, zero value, and out-of-range — are evaluated together as a combined rule. If any one of these conditions is true, a single unified error response is triggered: the error flag is set, the standard error message is displayed, and the Admin Menu screen is redisplayed for the user to correct their entry.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Set Error Flag
Display Error Message:
Please enter a valid option number...

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has submitted the Admin Menu screen with an option value that has been normalized into WS-OPTION
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the combined condition: WS-OPTION IS NOT NUMERIC, OR WS-OPTION equals zero (ZEROS), OR WS-OPTION is greater than the total count of available administrative options (CDEMO-ADMIN-OPT-COUNT) — and at least one of these conditions is true
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to 'Y' (WS-ERR-FLG = 'Y'), sets the error message to 'Please enter a valid option number...', and invokes the Admin Menu screen display routine (SEND-MENU-SCREEN) so the menu is redrawn with the error message visible to the user

rules.rule_name: Redisplay Admin Menu Screen After Invalid Option Entry
rules.rule_description: When an invalid option is entered on the Admin Menu, the user is not navigated away. Instead, the Admin Menu screen is refreshed and redisplayed with the error message, allowing the user to correct their selection.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Return to Admin Menu Screen with Error Message Displayed

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has entered an invalid option on the Admin Menu screen (non-numeric, zero, or out of range), and the error flag has been set with the message 'Please enter a valid option number...'
acceptance_criteria.When: The system invokes the Admin Menu screen send routine (SEND-MENU-SCREEN), which populates the screen header with current date, current time, transaction ID, and program name, builds the list of available menu options, places the error message in the error message display field (ERRMSGO), and sends the fully refreshed Admin Menu screen to the user
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Admin Menu screen is redrawn and presented to the user with all menu options visible and the error message 'Please enter a valid option number...' displayed, prompting the user to enter a valid selection

rules.rule_name: Skip Navigation When Validation Errors Are Present
rules.rule_description: Before attempting to navigate to any administrative function, the system must confirm that no validation errors were raised during option input processing. If errors exist, navigation is suppressed and the user remains on the Admin Menu.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Any Validation Errors Present?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has entered a menu option on the Admin Menu screen and pressed Enter, and one or more validation errors have been flagged during option input processing (error flag is set to ON)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates whether any validation errors are present before proceeding with navigation
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must NOT attempt to navigate to any administrative program; the user remains on the Admin Menu screen with the previously displayed error message intact

rules.rule_name: Check Whether Selected Admin Program Is Installed and Available
rules.rule_description: Before transferring control to the selected administrative program, the system must verify that the program associated with the chosen menu option is a real, installed program and not a placeholder. Programs marked as 'DUMMY' are considered unavailable.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is Selected Program Available and Installed?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has entered a valid menu option number (numeric, non-zero, within the allowed range) with no validation errors, and the system has identified the program name mapped to that option
acceptance_criteria.When: The system checks whether the first 5 characters of the selected option's associated program name equal 'DUMMY'
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the program name does NOT start with 'DUMMY', the program is considered installed and available, and navigation proceeds; if the program name starts with 'DUMMY', the program is considered unavailable, the message 'This option is not installed...' is displayed in green on the Admin Menu screen, and the user remains on the Admin Menu without any navigation occurring

rules.rule_name: Record Current Transaction as the Originating Transaction Before Navigation
rules.rule_description: Before transferring control to the selected administrative program, the system must capture and store the current transaction identifier as the originating transaction. This preserves the navigation trail so the destination program knows where the user came from.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Record Current Transaction ID as the Originating Transaction

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has selected a valid, installed administrative menu option with no validation errors, and the system is preparing to transfer control to the selected program
acceptance_criteria.When: The system records the originating transaction context prior to navigation
acceptance_criteria.Then: The current transaction ID (WS-TRANID) must be stored as the originating transaction identifier (CDEMO-FROM-TRANID) in the shared session communication area, so the destination program can identify the source transaction

rules.rule_name: Record Current Program as the Originating Program Before Navigation
rules.rule_description: Before transferring control to the selected administrative program, the system must capture and store the current program name as the originating program. This maintains the navigation breadcrumb so the destination program knows which program initiated the call.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Record Current Program Name as the Originating Program

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has selected a valid, installed administrative menu option with no validation errors, and the current transaction ID has already been recorded as the originating transaction
acceptance_criteria.When: The system records the originating program context prior to navigation
acceptance_criteria.Then: The current program name (WS-PGMNAME) must be stored as the originating program name (CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM) in the shared session communication area, so the destination program can identify which program transferred control to it

rules.rule_name: Reset Program Context to Fresh State Before Navigation
rules.rule_description: Before transferring control to the selected administrative program, the system must reset the program context indicator to zero. This ensures the destination program starts in a clean, initial state rather than inheriting any prior processing context.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Reset Program Context to Fresh State

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has selected a valid, installed administrative menu option with no validation errors, and both the originating transaction ID and originating program name have been recorded in the session communication area
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares the session context for handoff to the destination program
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program context value (CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT) in the shared session communication area must be set to zero (ZEROS), signaling to the destination program that it should initialize itself as if being entered for the first time

rules.rule_name: Transfer Control to Selected Administrative Program with Session Context
rules.rule_description: Once all pre-navigation steps are complete (validation passed, program confirmed as installed, originating context recorded, program context reset), the system transfers full control to the administrative program associated with the user's selected menu option, passing the complete session communication area.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Transfer Control to Selected Admin Program with Session Context

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has selected a valid, installed administrative menu option with no validation errors, the originating transaction ID and program name have been recorded, and the program context has been reset to zero
acceptance_criteria.When: The system executes the navigation to the selected administrative program
acceptance_criteria.Then: Control must be fully transferred to the program identified by the selected option's mapped program name (CDEMO-ADMIN-OPT-PGMNAME for the chosen option index), and the complete session communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) containing the originating transaction, originating program, and reset program context must be passed to the destination program; the Admin Menu program ceases execution at this point

rules.rule_name: Display 'Not Installed' Message and Return to Admin Menu When Program Is Unavailable
rules.rule_description: When a user selects a menu option whose associated program is marked as unavailable (DUMMY), the system must inform the user that the option is not yet available and keep them on the Admin Menu screen without navigating away.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: End: No Navigation Return to Admin Menu

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has entered a valid menu option number (numeric, non-zero, within the allowed range) with no validation errors, but the program associated with the selected option is marked as 'DUMMY' (not installed)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system determines that the selected option's program is not available for navigation
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must display the message 'This option is not installed...' in green color on the Admin Menu screen, redisplay the full Admin Menu (including header with current date, time, transaction ID, program name, and all available menu options), and the user must remain on the Admin Menu screen with no transfer of control to any other program

rules.rule_name: Identify Uninstalled Menu Option Marked as DUMMY
rules.rule_description: Determines whether the program associated with the selected admin menu option is a placeholder (DUMMY), indicating it has not yet been implemented or installed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is Selected Program Marked as DUMMY?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has selected a valid admin menu option number on the Admin Menu screen and pressed Enter
acceptance_criteria.When: The system looks up the program name associated with the selected option and checks whether the first 5 characters of that program name equal 'DUMMY'
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the program name starts with 'DUMMY', the system skips the program transfer and proceeds to display an informational message; if the program name does NOT start with 'DUMMY', the system proceeds to transfer control to that program

rules.rule_name: Transfer Control to Active Installed Program
rules.rule_description: When the selected menu option maps to a real, installed program (not marked as DUMMY), the system records the originating transaction and program context, then transfers full control to the selected program, passing the current session data.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Transfer Control to Selected Program

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has selected a valid admin menu option and the associated program name does not start with 'DUMMY'
acceptance_criteria.When: The system confirms the program is active and available
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system records the current transaction ID as the originating transaction, records the current program name as the originating program, resets the program context to zero, and transfers full control to the selected option's program along with the current session communication area

rules.rule_name: Clear Existing Message Before Displaying Uninstalled Notice
rules.rule_description: Before building and displaying the 'not installed' informational message, any previously displayed message on the Admin Menu screen is cleared to ensure only the current informational message is shown.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Clear any existing message

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has determined that the selected menu option's program is either marked as DUMMY or not found in the system
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares to display the uninstalled option notice
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system clears the message field (sets it to spaces) before populating it with the new informational message

rules.rule_name: Set Message Display Color to Green for Uninstalled Option Notice
rules.rule_description: When informing the user that a selected menu option is not yet installed, the message is displayed in green color to indicate it is an informational notice rather than an error.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set Message Color to Green

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has determined that the selected menu option's program is either marked as DUMMY or not found in the system
acceptance_criteria.When: The system sets the display attributes for the message field on the Admin Menu screen
acceptance_criteria.Then: The message color attribute for the error/info message field on the Admin Menu screen is set to green, distinguishing it as an informational message

rules.rule_name: Build 'Not Installed' Informational Message for Uninstalled Option
rules.rule_description: When a selected admin menu option is not available (program is DUMMY or not found), the system constructs a specific informational message to notify the user.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Build Message: 'This option is not installed...'

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has determined that the selected menu option's program is either marked as DUMMY or not found in the system, and the message field has been cleared
acceptance_criteria.When: The system builds the notification message
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system constructs the message by concatenating the text 'This option ' with 'is not installed ...' and stores it in the message field to be displayed on the Admin Menu screen

rules.rule_name: Display Admin Menu Screen with Green Informational Message for Uninstalled Option
rules.rule_description: After building the 'not installed' informational message in green, the Admin Menu screen is refreshed and redisplayed to the user, keeping them on the Admin Menu with the informational notice visible.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display Admin Menu Screen with Green Info Message

acceptance_criteria.Given: The 'This option is not installed...' message has been built and the message color has been set to green
acceptance_criteria.When: The system sends the updated Admin Menu screen to the user's terminal
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Admin Menu screen is fully refreshed (erased and redrawn) displaying the current date, time, transaction ID, program name, all available menu options, and the green informational message 'This option is not installed...'; the user remains on the Admin Menu screen

rules.rule_name: Handle System-Level Program Not Found for Selected Menu Option
rules.rule_description: When the system cannot locate the program associated with the selected admin menu option at the system level (program not registered or available), the user is informed with the same 'not installed' notice and kept on the Admin Menu.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Program Found in System?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has selected a valid admin menu option and the system attempts to transfer control to the associated program
acceptance_criteria.When: The system cannot find the specified program (program is not registered or available in the system)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system clears any existing message, sets the message color to green, builds the message 'This option is not installed...', displays the Admin Menu screen with this green informational message, and returns control to the same Admin Menu transaction with the current session data preserved — the user remains on the Admin Menu

rules.rule_name: Redirect Unauthenticated User to Sign-On Screen
rules.rule_description: When a user attempts to access the Admin Menu without an active session context, the system must redirect them to the Sign-On screen to ensure only authenticated users can access administrative functions.

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user attempts to access the Admin Menu and no active session context exists (no communication area has been passed from a prior transaction)
acceptance_criteria.When: The Admin Menu program is invoked without any prior session data
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the originating program reference to the Sign-On screen program 'COSGN00C' and immediately initiates a return to the Sign-On screen, preventing unauthenticated access to the Admin Menu

rules.rule_name: User Requests Exit from Admin Menu via PF3

rules.rule_name: Default Sign-On Target Program When Not Specified

acceptance_criteria.Then: The system automatically defaults the target program to the standard Sign-On screen program 'COSGN00C' before proceeding with the transfer

rules.rule_name: Use Pre-Set Sign-On Target Program When Already Specified
rules.rule_description: When a target Sign-On program has already been explicitly set prior to the return action, the system uses that pre-set destination without overriding it.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is about to transfer control back to the Sign-On screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The target Sign-On program destination has already been set to a valid program name (not empty and not low-values)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system retains the existing target program value 'COSGN00C' and proceeds with the transfer using that destination without modification

rules.rule_name: Transfer Control to Sign-On Screen
rules.rule_description: Once the target Sign-On program is confirmed (either defaulted or pre-set), the system transfers full control to the Sign-On screen program, effectively ending the Admin Menu session and redirecting the user.

rules.rule_name: Detect Unsupported Key Press on Admin Menu Screen
rules.rule_description: When a user presses any key other than Enter or PF3 on the Admin Menu screen, the system identifies it as an unsupported/invalid key and triggers the error handling flow.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is Key Enter or PF3?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the Admin Menu screen and has an active session with a loaded communication area
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses any key that is neither the Enter key nor the PF3 key
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system identifies the key press as unsupported and proceeds to set an error condition, preventing any normal menu processing from occurring

rules.rule_name: Set Error Flag ON for Invalid Key Press
rules.rule_description: When an unsupported key is pressed on the Admin Menu screen, the system activates an internal error flag to indicate that an error condition exists, which will suppress normal processing and trigger error display.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set Error Flag to ON

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the Admin Menu screen and has pressed a key that is neither Enter nor PF3
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the key pressed and determines it falls under the unsupported key category
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag (WS-ERR-FLG) to 'Y' (ON), marking the current interaction as an error state so that no menu option processing is attempted

rules.rule_name: Load Invalid Key Error Message
rules.rule_description: When an unsupported key is pressed on the Admin Menu screen, the system loads the standard invalid key error message from the application message configuration into the screen message field to inform the user.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Load Invalid Key Error Message

acceptance_criteria.Given: The error flag has been set to ON due to an unsupported key press on the Admin Menu screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares to redisplay the Admin Menu screen with an error notification
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system loads the standard invalid key error message (CCDA-MSG-INVALID-KEY) into the screen message field (WS-MESSAGE), which will be presented to the user on the Admin Menu screen

rules.rule_name: Display Admin Menu Screen with Invalid Key Error Message
rules.rule_description: After detecting an unsupported key press and loading the error message, the system redisplays the Admin Menu screen — including the current date, time, transaction ID, program name, all available menu options, and the invalid key error message — so the user can retry with a valid key.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display Admin Menu Screen with Error Message

acceptance_criteria.Given: The error flag is ON and the invalid key error message (CCDA-MSG-INVALID-KEY) has been loaded into the message field (WS-MESSAGE), and the user is on the Admin Menu screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The system sends the Admin Menu screen back to the user
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system displays the Admin Menu screen (COADM1A from mapset COADM01) with: (1) the current date in MM/DD/YY format, (2) the current time in HH:MM:SS format, (3) the current transaction ID and program name in the header, (4) all available admin menu options formatted as '[Option Number]. [Option Name]' for up to 10 options, and (5) the invalid key error message visible in the error message area (ERRMSGO), with the entire screen erased and redrawn so the user can view the error and attempt a valid key press

key_functionalities.title: Missing Program Error Handling
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    A([Trigger: Selected Program\nCannot Be Found or Is Not Installed])

    C[Set Message Color to Green\nIndicating Informational Message]

    E[Display Admin Menu Screen\nwith Green Informational Message]
    F([End: User Remains on\nAdmin Menu Screen])

rules.rule_name: Clear Existing Message Before Displaying Not-Installed Notice
rules.rule_description: Before displaying the 'option not installed' informational message, any previously displayed message on the Admin Menu screen must be cleared to ensure no stale or conflicting message content is shown to the user.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Clear Any Existing Message
Reset Message Area to Spaces

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has selected an administrative menu option and the system determines the associated program is either not found or marked as not installed (DUMMY)
acceptance_criteria.When: The missing program error handling process is triggered
acceptance_criteria.Then: The message area (WS-MESSAGE) must be reset to spaces, removing any previously displayed message content before the new informational message is built

rules.rule_name: Set Informational Message Color to Green for Not-Installed Notice
rules.rule_description: When an administrative menu option is not installed, the message displayed to the user must be rendered in green to visually distinguish it as an informational notice rather than a critical error.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Set Message Color to Green
Indicating Informational Message

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has determined that the selected administrative menu option's program is not installed or cannot be found
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares to display the not-installed notice on the Admin Menu screen
acceptance_criteria.Then: The error message color attribute (ERRMSGC) on the Admin Menu output screen (COADM1AO) must be set to green (DFHGREEN), indicating the message is informational in nature

rules.rule_name: Build Not-Installed Informational Message for Uninstalled Admin Option
rules.rule_description: When a user selects an administrative menu option whose program is either marked as a placeholder (DUMMY) or cannot be found by the system, a specific informational message must be constructed and presented to the user explaining that the option is not available.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Build Informational Message:
'This option is not installed...'

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user selects an administrative menu option and the system identifies that the option's associated program name begins with 'DUMMY' (first 5 characters equal 'DUMMY'), OR the system cannot locate the program at runtime
acceptance_criteria.When: The not-installed message is being prepared for display
acceptance_criteria.Then: The message area (WS-MESSAGE) must be populated with the concatenated text 'This option is not installed ...' by combining the literal 'This option ' with the literal 'is not installed ...' using full field size as the delimiter

rules.rule_name: Display Admin Menu Screen with Not-Installed Informational Message
rules.rule_description: After building the not-installed informational message and setting its color to green, the Admin Menu screen must be refreshed and redisplayed to the user, showing the message along with the full menu header (current date, time, transaction ID, program name) and all available menu options.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Display Admin Menu Screen
with Green Informational Message

acceptance_criteria.Given: The not-installed message has been built in WS-MESSAGE and the message color has been set to green on the Admin Menu output screen (COADM1AO)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system invokes the Send Menu Screen process
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Admin Menu screen must be fully refreshed by: (1) populating the header with current date in MM/DD/YY format, current time in HH:MM:SS format, the current transaction ID, and the current program name; (2) building and displaying all available administrative menu options (up to 10) formatted as '[Option Number]. [Option Name]'; (3) placing the not-installed message into the screen's error message field (ERRMSGO of COADM1AO); and (4) sending the screen to the user with full erase of previous content

rules.rule_name: Retain User on Admin Menu After Not-Installed Program Error
rules.rule_description: After displaying the not-installed informational message, the user must be kept on the Admin Menu screen within the same transaction session, preserving the full session context so they can make another menu selection.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
End: User Remains on
Admin Menu Screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Admin Menu screen has been redisplayed with the green 'This option is not installed ...' message after a program-not-found condition was triggered
acceptance_criteria.When: The system completes the missing program error handling process
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must return control to the same administrative menu transaction (identified by WS-TRANID) and pass the current session context (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) forward, ensuring the user remains on the Admin Menu screen and their session state is fully preserved for their next interaction

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user attempts to access the Admin Menu program
Acceptance_Criteria.When: No active session context exists (communication area length is zero)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the origin program to 'COSGN00C' and redirects the user to the Sign-On screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: New Session Detection and Sign-On Redirect
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user attempts to access the Admin Menu without an active session context, the system redirects them to the Sign-On screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has an active session and navigates to the Admin Menu for the first time
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program detects it has not been previously entered (CDEMO-PGM-REENTER is not set)
