all_rules.Rule_Description: After capturing and trimming the user's menu option input, any spaces that still remain within the option value must be replaced with zeros. This ensures that a partially blank or whitespace-padded entry is normalized to a numeric-looking value before validation. For example, a single character entered as '1 ' becomes '10' after replacement.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has entered a menu option value on the Admin Menu screen, and the trailing-space trimming step has already been performed, resulting in a captured option value stored in the working option input field (WS-OPTION-X)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system inspects the captured option input field (WS-OPTION-X) and finds no space characters remaining within the value
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system leaves the option input field (WS-OPTION-X) unchanged and proceeds directly to store the value as the cleaned option ready for validation

all_rules.Rule_Name: No Spaces Present — Option Value Passes Through Unchanged
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the captured menu option input contains no remaining spaces after the trimming step, the value is already clean and requires no replacement. It is passed directly to the next step for storage and validation without modification.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The menu option input field (WS-OPTION-X) has been fully normalized — trailing spaces trimmed and any remaining spaces replaced with zeros
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system is ready to proceed to option validation
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system copies the cleaned and normalized option value from the working input field (WS-OPTION-X) into the active option selection field (WS-OPTION), making it the definitive value to be used for all validation and navigation logic

all_rules.Rule_Name: Store Cleaned Option Value as the Active Selection for Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: Once the option input has been normalized (spaces replaced with zeros where applicable), the cleaned value must be stored into the active menu option field (WS-OPTION). This field is the definitive value that will be used in all subsequent validation checks to determine whether the user's selection is a valid admin menu option.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The cleaned and normalized menu option value has been stored in the active option selection field (WS-OPTION)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to display or redisplay the Admin Menu screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system moves the cleaned option value from the active option selection field (WS-OPTION) into the screen output option display field (OPTIONO of COADM1AO), so that the user sees the normalized value that the system will use for validation and processing

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Cleaned Option Value Back on the Admin Menu Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the option value has been cleaned and stored, the normalized value must be reflected back on the Admin Menu screen in the option display field. This ensures the user sees exactly what value the system has recorded as their selection, providing transparency and consistency between what was entered and what will be processed.

description:
COADM01C is a CICS online program that serves as the Administrative Menu for the CardDemo application, presenting admin users with a list of available administrative options and routing them to the appropriate sub-programs based on their selection. The program handles user input validation, displays up to 10 menu options dynamically built from a common area, and transfers control to the selected option's program via XCTL or returns the user to the sign-on screen. It operates as a Main/Driver program, receiving control from the sign-on screen and dispatching to other administrative modules.
- **Execution Environment**: Online (CICS) - **Database Access**: None - **MQ Calls**: No - **Module Type**: Main/Driver module
### Key Functionalities: 1: Session Validation - Check if the user session is active by verifying the communication area. If no session exists, redirect the user to the Sign-On screen to authenticate before accessing the Admin Menu. 2: Initial Admin Menu Display - On the first entry to the Admin Menu, initialize the screen and display the Admin Menu to the user with all available administrative options populated. 3: Admin Menu Screen Rendering - Build and send the Admin Menu screen to the user, including current date, current time, application title, program name, transaction ID, and all available menu options. 4: Header Information Population - Populate the screen header with the current date (MM/DD/YY format), current time (HH:MM:SS format), application titles, transaction ID, and program name for display on the Admin Menu screen. 5: Menu Options Construction - Dynamically build and display up to 10 administrative menu options on the screen by combining each option number and option name from the configured list of admin options. 6: User Input Capture - Receive and capture the user's input from the Admin Menu screen, including the option number entered by the user. 7: Enter Key Processing - Process the user's menu selection when the Enter key is pressed, including reading the entered option value and preparing it for validation. 8: Menu Option Validation - Validate the user-entered option to ensure it is numeric, non-zero, and within the valid range of available administrative options. Display an error message if the option is invalid. 9: Navigate to Selected Admin Function - Transfer control to the selected administrative program based on the user's valid menu option selection, passing the communication area to maintain session context. 10: Uninstalled Option Handling - Display an informational message in green indicating that the selected menu option is not yet installed, when the selected program is marked as a dummy or is not available. 11: Return to Sign-On Screen - Transfer control back to the Sign-On screen when the user presses PF3 or when no valid session exists, effectively logging the user out of the Admin Menu. 12: Invalid Key Handling - Display an error message to the user when an unsupported key (other than Enter or PF3) is pressed on the Admin Menu screen, prompting the user to use a valid key. 13: Missing Program Error Handling - When a selected administrative program cannot be found or is not installed, display a green informational message indicating the option is not installed and return the user to the Admin Menu.
